title: Continuous cellular automata show the same complexity as discrete ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Continuous cellular automata show the same complexity as discrete ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cellular automata whose cells take a continuous range of gray levels, updated by simple maps of the neighborhood average, show the same kind of complexity as ordinary discrete cellular automata, and can even show localized structures.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: despite the presence of continuous gray levels, the behavior that is produced exhibits the same kind of complexity that we have seen in many ordinary cellular automata and other systems with discrete underlying elements.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Continuous Cellular Automata” (from p. 155), p. 157. Scope: one-dimensional continuous-valued cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-22: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named class is directly simulable and the existential presence of complex or localized behavior can be reproduced under precision checks. Standard computation can distinguish robust structures from approximation artifacts within weeks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Implement the specified continuous-valued local update maps, run them at increasing numerical precision, and quantify spatiotemporal complexity and persistent localized structures using the same metrics as discrete automata. Precision-stable examples confirm the existential comparison.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Same kind of complexity requires a cross-system metric.

Numerical precision and discretization can create artifacts.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: These systems are discrete in space and time with a continuous cell value, and the stated update rules are exact maps that public arithmetic can iterate at large size. Reproducing aperiodic evolution and localized structures would confirm the examples; a drift to a simple attractor would refute them. Matching the open-ended phrase 'the same kind of complexity' as ordinary cellular automata is a further, less sharp comparison.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate one-dimensional continuous cellular automata, including fractional part of 3/2 times the neighborhood average and addition of a constant modulo 1, in exact rational or high-precision arithmetic. Persistent aperiodicity and particle-like localized structures support the claim; collapse to periodic or spatially uniform evolution under exact arithmetic would refute the examples.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'The same kind of complexity' is a qualitative comparison and can be satisfied by loose resemblance.

Floating-point artifacts can create or destroy fine structure, so the run has to be checked in exact or validated arithmetic.

data existence: 0.85
